name: hora Calendar
soft_passes: #2 monogram overspills the safe zone (tail near bottom edge, ascender into the band, mass low-right) — signature-scale but not optically centered
#4 black monogram survives 16px but the ruled lines, the '18' and the coral glow smear away — the calendar meaning is lost at Dock/Spotlight size
#8 coral ground-glow behind an ink-black letter is decorative, unmotivated by the flat front-lit model
#12 contains a numeral '18' and a letterform h — both defensible (Apple Calendar's date convention; single-letter monogram exception) but not strictly text-free
failures: #10 not authored for Liquid Glass — colour-dependent ink-black-on-white monogram + red band won't produce clean dark/clear/tinted/mono variants; era mismatch with macOS 26

palette.background: two-zone: coral header ramp #F55552->#F96D6B over paper field #F1F2F3->#FFFFFF with warm coral bleed #FFEAE9 at bottom

light_model: near-flat front-lit; only two events — a soft short drop-shadow lifting the black script off the paper, and a coral ground-glow halo behind the monogram base; no specular, no refraction
layer_stack: black brush-script h monogram + soft drop-shadow
devices: signature-scale hand-inked brush-script monogram breaking across all layers
flattened calendar-page quote (coral header + ruled agenda lines + grey date numeral)
rhymes_hint: hand-lettered monogram-on-stationery brand icons crossed with the ruled-paper + date-number calendar/notes family (Apple Calendar date-on-icon, Fantastical date block, Apple Notes ruling) — indie-warm, ink-forward, high-contrast register
notes: Source is a 512x512 PRE-MASKED RGBA render (squircle corners already transparent), NOT the 1024 full-bleed unmasked master — full-bleed mask authoring unverifiable, corner radius baked by exporter, gradients compression-flattened; hex (measured) from this render. Era is Big Sur flat language carrying a SEMIOTIC (not material) skeuomorphic quote of a calendar page — no texture realism, so classified big-sur rather than skeuomorphic-quote. Strong icon<->brand coherence: cover reuses the same coral-red family and the same script-h-in-a-rounded-badge as the wordmark lockup. For synthesis: first icon in corpus, no cluster yet; the oversized-hand-lettered-monogram device and the date-numeral-on-calendar-icon convention are both candidate recurring devices to watch for.
